themes_detail.label: Dead Animals Surge
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 8 this week versus a baseline of 1.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 611% increase (z-score: 5.04)—suggesting potential public health or sanitation system breakdown in CD 404 this week.
evidence: 8 dead animal complaints this week vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (611% spike)
Z-score of 5.04 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Timing coincides with warm weather and potential sanitation response gaps
reporting_angles: Investigate whether Sanitation Department is understaffed or delayed in responding to CD 404
Interview residents about whether they've noticed rodent/pest activity or degraded street conditions preceding animal deaths

themes_detail.label: Homeless Encampments Spike
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 17 this week compared to a baseline of 3.9 per week—a 339% increase (z-score: 4.84)—reflecting a sudden surge in homelessness visibility that aligns with repeated DHS budget requests from the community board.
evidence: 17 encampment complaints this week vs. 3.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (339% spike)
Z-score of 4.84 indicates high statistical significance
Community board has filed repeated budget requests for DHS homeless services, suggesting chronic unmet need
reporting_angles: Profile residents in visible encampments to understand why CD 404 (high transit hub, near airport) is becoming a concentration point
Examine whether DHS emergency shelter capacity in Queens is adequate or whether street homelessness is being pushed to this district

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Vandalism Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged to 31 three weeks ago versus a baseline of 2.4 per week—a 1205% spike (z-score: 21.74)—representing the most statistically extreme anomaly in the dataset and indicating organized or gang-related tagging activity.
evidence: 31 graffiti complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1205% spike)
Z-score of 21.74—the highest statistical anomaly in the entire dataset
Spike is 3 weeks old; unclear if it has sustained or been addressed
reporting_angles: Determine whether this was a coordinated tagging event or sustained gang/vandalism activity; map complaint locations for hot spots
Check NYPD crime data and gang intelligence to see if graffiti correlates with territorial disputes or organized crews

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints jumped to 4 last week versus a baseline of 0.8 per week—a 433% spike (z-score: 4.91)—likely reflecting unlicensed dispensaries or community pushback against legal retail opening in this week.
evidence: 4 cannabis retailer complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% spike)
Likely driver: new licensed dispensaries opening or unlicensed operators operating in CD 404
reporting_angles: Identify which cannabis retail licenses were recently approved or opened in CD 404; interview community board about opposition
Check SCA/DOH enforcement data for unlicensed dispensaries and social equity applicant status

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Disturbances
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints spiked to 17 last week versus a baseline of 3.0 per week—a 467% increase (z-score: 4.95)—suggesting either larger public gatherings or organized events (possibly weather-related) in CD 404's parks.
evidence: 17 park noise complaints last week vs. 3.0 weekly average (467% spike)
Z-score of 4.95 indicates high statistical significance
Community board has repeatedly requested park reconstruction/upgrades, suggesting infrastructure or management gaps
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are generating complaints (Elmhurst Park, Astoria Park branches); check for permitted events or permit violations
Interview Parks Dept about noise enforcement capacity and whether parks lack adequate lighting/programming that might be driving late-night gatherings
